It's actually very simple. Health care is extremely inelastic and the barriers to entry on almost every part of the industry are very high. If you let the market sort it out without enforcing competition you'll get natural monopolies. In general, in their effects, monopolies are as bad as socialism. The health care industry is particularly bad to give to laissez faire goings on.

Free market supporters are generally correct on a wide variety of economic topics. But all choices are not well-informed and it's not okay for a human to fail due to lack of support. The free market works only where competition is active. A person with a heart attack isn't going to be able to collect bids on the four nearest hospitals. And health care is an extremely complex topic with lots of hidden information even before health care companies start lying.

A heartless classical economist would say "Bob chose not to spend his money on health insurance. Now he's dying. Tough"

Countries with socialized healthcare miss out on the benefits of competition, but there are huge benefits to having a healthy population. Economic benefits and even national security benefits. When Bob dies society loses the 12 years of school and the cost to support, protect, and raise a child. Or, if you look at the other side, the full value of his future work and innovation. The health care industry is insulated from these costs. On the national security side a fully nationalized healthcare system can respond better and faster to epidemics and a healthy nation can rapidly field more healthy young people in the case of, Goddess forbid, war.

Furthermore sick people don't just quietly die. They wait until they're REALLY sick and then go to an emergency room which is legally obligated to care for them. That is often more expensive. And finally, sick people may make others sick.

All things considered nationalized, single-payer healthcare would greatly drop the cost of health care in the US even though the poor would have to be brought on board.

But more importantly, caring for the poor and sick is the right thing to do.
